headline: Markets now expect a Bank of Canada hike next week after Macklem warned on oil-driven inflation. A surprise drop in UK unemployment lifted the pound before Wednesday's inflation test.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar was steady overnight, near 102 on the index, after ending a two-day slide on Monday. A US official denied Iran's claim that US forces hit its Konarak base, which took some heat out of the story. Housing data at 7:30 AM CT is today's only US test.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Asia was calm for the dollar. The index held near 102 and the 10-year yield sat flat near 5.13%, after Monday's oil-driven rise. A US official denied that American forces struck Iran's Konarak naval base; Iran's navy still says two projectiles hit a gun position there, and US Central Command has not commented. With no confirmation and no new strike overnight, the haven and oil channels for the dollar did not get a fresh push. Fed pricing barely moved: October is still seen as a hold, and markets put a December hike at roughly 4 in 5. Thread: yesterday's edition said the dollar's support came from others' trouble and from oil lifting yields, not new US strength. That still holds; the dollar moved more against the pound this morning than on any US news. What it means: the dollar is waiting. Today's housing starts and permits are a second look at the squeeze high mortgage rates put on housing after Monday's 14-year low in builder confidence. A weak print feeds the 'Fed should wait' side but rarely moves the dollar much on its own. The lens: are US yields being pushed by oil, or by the Fed?
chapters.fx: What to watch: US housing starts and permits 7:30 AM CT; pending home sales 9 AM CT; API crude stocks 3:30 PM CT; any US or Iranian follow-up on Konarak. The Fed stays in its quiet period until the October 27–28 meeting.
numbers: Fed: Oct hold ~84%; Dec hike ~83% (CME FedWatch)

scenarios.base: If housing data is soft but orderly and the Konarak story fades, the dollar drifts with yields and the euro.
scenarios.bull: If the US confirms a strike or Iran retaliates, oil and yields rise and the dollar gains on both the haven and the rate channel.
scenarios.bear: If housing data is weak enough to cool December hike bets, yields ease and the dollar gives back Monday's lift.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro steadied near $1.123 overnight as curfews were imposed in several French cities. German factory-gate prices ran hotter than expected, keeping the ECB's December hike case alive. Today's budget revenue vote in Paris is the euro's real test.
chapters.meaning: What changed: two things. First, France: curfews went into place in several cities after nationwide protests, and the gap between French and German 10-year borrowing costs widened by about 10bp on Monday to around 147bp. Second, German producer prices, run through the four beats: (1) this is what German firms charge for goods as they leave the factory, an early read on costs that reach shoppers later; (2) prices rose 1.9% in September alone against 1.5% expected, and 6.7% from a year ago against 6.2% expected, the fastest since March 2023; (3) that is energy from the Gulf conflict working its way into the supply chain, so euro-area inflation, already near 3.8% against the ECB's 2% goal, has more pressure coming; (4) for the euro, that keeps the ECB on course for a December hike, which supports the currency through rates, but France's stress is pulling the other way through risk. The euro held near $1.123 in Asia. Thread: yesterday's edition named today's vote as the next test; Pepperstone notes the euro is holding up because traders still see France as a French problem, not a euro-area one. What it means: the ECB's hike case is getting stronger while France's trouble gets louder. The lens: does French stress stay inside France's bond market, or spread to the euro itself?
chapters.fx: What to watch: ZEW investor sentiment 4 AM CT; France's revenue-section budget vote Tuesday; Bundesbank's Nagel 2:15 AM CT Wednesday; Lagarde Wednesday; Moody's France review Friday.
numbers: ECB: Oct hold ~97%; Dec hike likely

scenarios.base: If the revenue vote passes without big concessions, the spread steadies and the euro holds near $1.12.
scenarios.bull: If the vote passes cleanly and protests ease, the spread narrows and the euro's rate support from the ECB shows through.
scenarios.bear: If the vote fails or unrest spreads beyond France, the spread widens and the euro tests last week's 16-month low near $1.111.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: UK unemployment fell unexpectedly to 4.7%, and regular pay growth edged up instead of cooling. The pound rose about 0.3% to near $1.334, its best level in over a week. Wednesday's inflation report is now the last big test before the November hike.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the jobs report, through the four beats. (1) It measures how many people are out of work and how fast pay is rising. (2) Unemployment fell to 4.7% from 4.9%, where it was expected to stay; regular pay growth ticked up to 3.7% against 3.6% expected; but jobless-benefit claims rose by 30,000, more than expected, and total pay including bonuses slowed. (3) A firmer job market and steady pay mean wage-driven inflation is not fading on its own, which is the Bank of England's main worry. (4) For the pound: a BoE under more pressure to act means higher rates for longer, which draws money into sterling. A November hike was already almost fully priced, so the gain is about December. The pound rose about 0.3% to near $1.334. Thread: yesterday's edition set up tonight's jobs data and Wednesday's inflation as the real test; the first half passed in the hawkish direction. What it means: the pound now leans on Wednesday. Inflation near the expected 3.4% keeps the November hike locked in; a hotter number would bring a December follow-up into play. The lens: is the BoE's next move after November a second hike or a pause?
chapters.fx: What to watch: 10-year gilt auction about 4:30 AM CT; MPC member Greene at noon CT; UK inflation 1 AM CT Wednesday; Bailey speaks 8 AM CT Wednesday; the budget on October 28.
numbers: Regular pay +3.7% vs 3.6% expected; claimant count +30.3K vs 19.4K
BoE Nov 5 hike ~95% priced; UK CPI Wed ~3.4% expected

scenarios.base: If inflation lands near 3.4%, the November hike stays locked in and the pound holds today's gain into the budget.
scenarios.bull: If inflation runs hotter, markets price a December follow-up and the pound extends.
scenarios.bear: If inflation surprises low, the jobs beat fades from view and the pound gives back the gain.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: Quiet for the yen: flat near 158.6 per dollar overnight with US yields steady. No new Bank of Japan signal; Friday's inflation report is the next real test.
chapters.meaning: What changed: little. USD/JPY sat flat near 158.6 in Asia as the US 10-year yield held near 5.13%. There was no new BoJ guidance overnight; markets still see October as a hold and December as the likely hike. Thread: yesterday's edition said the yen weakens when oil pushes US yields up; overnight neither moved. What it means: the yen is pinned by the gap between US and Japanese rates until Friday's inflation report or the BoJ's October 29–30 forecasts change the picture. The lens: is Japan's inflation strong enough to bring the BoJ's next hike forward?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Japan trade balance 6:50 PM CT tonight; Japan national inflation Friday; BoJ October 29–30 (new forecasts); US 10-year yields; 160 per dollar, where Japan has stepped in before.
numbers: BoJ Oct 30: hold expected; Dec hike likely

scenarios.base: If US yields stay near 5.13%, USD/JPY holds below 160 into Friday's data.
scenarios.bull: If Japan's inflation beats or US yields fall, the gap narrows and the yen firms.
scenarios.bear: If oil and US yields climb again, the yen weakens toward 160, where intervention risk rises.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: Quiet for the franc: little changed near 0.825 per dollar and close to its strongest against the euro in three months. No Swiss news; France and the Gulf still set its tone.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no Swiss driver overnight. The franc held near 0.825 per dollar, and stayed close to Monday's three-month high against the euro as French stress kept a bid under havens. The US denial on Konarak removed some of Monday's Gulf-driven haven demand. Thread: yesterday's edition called it a two-way day, firm against the euro, softer against the dollar; that pattern held. What it means: the franc keeps moving on outside fear, while the SNB, at zero rates, has no reason to lean against it except a possible December cut. The lens: is outside fear rising faster than the SNB's appetite to cut?
chapters.fx: What to watch: France's budget vote Tuesday; any Gulf follow-up; the SNB's write-up of its last meeting Thursday.

scenarios.base: If France and the Gulf stay tense but contained, the franc drifts with the dollar.
scenarios.bull: If French stress spreads or the Gulf escalates, haven demand lifts the franc broadly.
scenarios.bear: If both risks fade, the haven bid drains and talk of an SNB cut weighs on the franc.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie held near 0.699, just under 70 US cents, after Monday's China-driven rally. China kept its lending rates unchanged as expected, so there was no new push. RBA Deputy Governor Hauser speaks at 5:30 PM CT.
chapters.meaning: What changed: China's banks held their benchmark lending rates for a 17th straight month, exactly as surveyed. After Monday's stronger growth figure, Beijing is in no hurry to ease, which is neutral for the Aussie: no extra stimulus, but no sign of trouble either. The Aussie edged up about 0.1% to near 0.699 in Asia as risk appetite recovered a little. Thread: yesterday's edition credited China's growth beat for the Aussie's best day among majors; the Aussie kept that gain overnight. What it means: the next driver is the RBA itself. Kent kept a November hike open but flagged a faster-loosening job market; Hauser tonight is the next read on which side wins. Positioning cuts both ways: hedge funds still lean toward the Aussie while long-term investors bet against it, so a bad turn in risk could hit it quickly. The lens: does the RBA see inflation or the job market as the bigger risk?
chapters.fx: What to watch: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser 5:30 PM CT; New Zealand inflation 4:45 PM CT Wednesday; Australia quarterly inflation October 28; RBA November 2–3.
numbers: CFTC: funds for AUD, real money strongly against

scenarios.base: If Hauser repeats Kent's two-sided message, the Aussie holds near 0.70 into the inflation reports.
scenarios.bull: If Hauser leans hawkish or risk appetite builds, November pricing firms and the Aussie clears 0.70.
scenarios.bear: If Hauser leans on the softer job market or stocks turn down, the Aussie gives back the China gain.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: Correction to yesterday: by Monday's close, markets had swung to expecting a Bank of Canada hike next week, about 87% priced, after Macklem warned oil would push inflation up. Several big banks changed their calls. The loonie firmed to near 1.409 per dollar.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the October 28 decision flipped. Yesterday's edition said a hike was unlikely after soft core inflation; that was stale by the close. On Saturday Macklem said the bank will raise its inflation forecast 'significantly' and that with oil around $100, inflation should drift up from about 3%. By Monday afternoon, swaps put the odds of a hike to 2.50% near 87%, up from about 70% earlier in the day, and BMO, RBC and Desjardins switched to calling a hike; a Bloomberg survey still leaned to a hold. Run through the four beats: (1) the signal is the bank's own forecast, not a data print; (2) markets moved from 'hold likely' to 'hike likely' in two days; (3) the BoC is saying it will act on where inflation is heading in six to twelve months, not on today's cool core measures; (4) for the loonie: a central bank willing to hike while others wait means higher Canadian yields, which pulls money in. USD/CAD fell for a fourth day to near 1.409, helped by firm oil. Thread: yesterday's edition said hike talk was limiting the loonie's downside; it has become the base case. What it means: with a hike mostly priced, a hold next week would now be the surprise. The lens: is the BoC set on acting before the data proves it?
chapters.fx: What to watch: oil into today's November WTI expiry; US housing data 7:30 AM CT; Canada retail sales later this week; BoC decision October 28.
numbers: Macklem: inflation to drift up from ~3% if oil stays ~$100
CFTC: hedge funds strongly against CAD

scenarios.base: If oil stays firm and BoC officials don't push back, the hike stays priced and the loonie holds its gains.
scenarios.bull: If oil climbs further or more forecasters switch to a hike, hedge funds' bets against the loonie get squeezed and it gains.
scenarios.bear: If oil drops or the BoC signals patience, the hike pricing unwinds and the loonie gives back the move.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: Swaps now give about an 80% chance the RBNZ hikes on October 28, firmer than the close call of last week. The kiwi was flat near 0.5665. Wednesday's inflation report decides whether that holds.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the RBNZ call firmed toward a hike. BBH notes swaps price about 80% odds of a quarter-point rise to 3.00% next week, and the major local banks lean the same way. The kiwi barely moved, near 0.5665, because the shift built up over several days rather than overnight. Thread: yesterday's edition called it a close call to be settled by Wednesday's inflation report; the market has moved ahead of the data. What it means: with a hike mostly priced, the inflation report now matters more if it is soft. Annual inflation is expected to ease to about 3.8%, close to the RBNZ's own forecast; a print in line keeps the hike on, a clearly softer one would put the hold back on the table and weigh on the kiwi. Hedge funds are betting against the kiwi, so a hawkish surprise could force them to cover. The lens: is New Zealand's inflation cooling fast enough to let the RBNZ wait?
chapters.fx: What to watch: Global Dairy Trade auction about 9:50 AM CT; New Zealand Q3 inflation 4:45 PM CT Wednesday; RBNZ October 28.
numbers: NZ Q3 CPI Wed: ~3.8% y/y expected (prior 4.1%)
CFTC: funds added to bets against NZD

scenarios.base: If dairy prices hold and inflation lands near 3.8%, the hike stays priced and the kiwi waits near 0.57.
scenarios.bull: If inflation runs hot, a hike is locked in and funds' bets against the kiwi get squeezed.
scenarios.bear: If inflation comes in clearly soft, hike pricing unwinds and the kiwi slips.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil held its supply premium overnight even after a US official denied striking Iran's Konarak base: Brent stayed near $110. The expiring US contract settled at a five-week high Monday, but the next one trades near $98.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Monday's settles came in two directions. Brent closed slightly lower at $109.55 on profit-taking near a five-month high, while US crude's November contract jumped 2.2% to $103.66 in thin trade before today's expiry. Overnight, a US official denied that American forces hit Konarak; Iran's navy maintains its account, and US Central Command has not commented. Iran's Revolutionary Guards declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, while the US Navy's regional commander said it remains open to commerce. Gulf crude flows have fallen to about 8.5m barrels a day from over 20m a week earlier (Kpler). Brent held near $110 into Tuesday and the more-traded December WTI contract sat near $98. Thread: yesterday's call said a US denial or silence would let the waiver-driven drop resume; it didn't, because the flow data and Hormuz claims kept the premium in place. What it means: for currencies, firm oil supports the loonie, keeps pressure on importers like the yen and euro, and keeps US yields elevated. The lens: are tankers moving through the Gulf again, or not?
chapters.fx: What to watch: November WTI expiry today; API inventories 3:30 PM CT; EIA inventories 9:30 AM CT Wednesday; Houthi activity around Saudi export routes; any US–Iran contact.
numbers: Gulf flows ~8.5m b/d vs 20m+ a week ago (Kpler)
CFTC: funds' oil bets among the weakest since 2015

scenarios.base: If Gulf flows stay low and the Konarak story fades, oil holds a supply premium with wide daily swings.
scenarios.bull: If Iran retaliates or Houthi strikes hit Saudi exports, the premium grows and Brent clears its five-month high.
scenarios.bear: If tanker traffic visibly recovers or US–Iran talks restart, the premium drains quickly.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold slipped to near $4,120 in early European trade, about $20 under Monday's close. US yields holding above 5.1% and December hike bets keep a lid on it. It stays in the lower half of its $4,100–4,200 range.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold extended Monday's dip to near $4,120. The pull is the same as yesterday: oil keeps US yields high, and gold pays no interest, so it loses appeal when bonds pay more. Markets still expect the Fed to hold in October and hike in December, which keeps that pressure in place. The US denial on Konarak also took a little of the conflict bid out. Thread: yesterday's edition said gold was stuck in its $4,100–4,200 range while December hike pricing held; it is now testing the bottom half of that range. What it means: gold is trading as a rate asset, not a fear asset, right now. A break below $4,100 would say yields are winning outright; a Gulf escalation that pulls yields down would flip it. The lens: which moves gold more this week, yields or fear?
chapters.fx: What to watch: US yields after housing data 7:30 AM CT; Gulf headlines; UK and New Zealand inflation for the global rate-hike mood.
numbers: CFTC: funds strongly for gold, trimmed

scenarios.bull: If US yields fall back or the Gulf escalates, gold heads back toward $4,200.
scenarios.bear: If oil and yields push higher, gold breaks below $4,100.
